title: Apex Experiential Scenario
description: A simulated, conversational practice experience: a Claude-driven role-play character a learner negotiates/leads/sells against, plus a Kolb-cycle debrief configuration. One scenario file realizes the 'learning by doing' layer for one or more module learning objectives.

moduleId.description: Must match a moduleId in index.json / module.schema.json.

modality.description: The kind of human interaction being simulated. Drives UI affordances and the debrief lens.

targetObjectiveIds.description: Learning-objective ids (from the module manifest) this scenario lets the learner practice. Preserves constructive alignment: practice is tied to the same objectives the module teaches and assesses.

linkedAssessmentIds.description: Assessment ids (from the module manifest) this scenario can serve as evidence for. Optional.

learnerBrief.description: What the LEARNER sees before the simulation starts. This is public.

givens.description: Facts/constraints the learner is handed (e.g. their own BATNA, budget, timeline).

skillsToPractice.description: Plain-language reminder of the moves to attempt, mapped to targetObjectiveIds.

character.description: The simulated human. 'persona' is public flavor; 'hiddenState' is NEVER shown to the learner and is injected only into the character agent's system prompt.

persona.description: Public-facing description of who the character appears to be. Visible to the learner.

voice.description: Tone/diction guidance for the character agent (e.g. 'clipped, transactional, mildly impatient').

hiddenState.description: The character's secret goals and parameters. Drives realistic, non-scripted behavior. WITHHELD from the learner; revealed in debrief.

batna.description: The character's own best alternative / walk-away.

reservationValue.description: The character's secret limit (e.g. the most they'll pay).

openingAnchor.description: The aggressive figure/position the character opens with.

concessionLogic.description: When and how the character yields, and to what learner moves.

tells.description: Observable cues the character emits when the learner does something effective (so a skilled learner can 'read the tide').

behaviorRules.description: Hard constraints on the character agent: stay in character, never reveal hiddenState, respond to specific learner moves in specific ways, don't coach.

difficulty.description: How hard the character pushes back. Lets one scenario scale across learner readiness.

successSignals.description: Observable, objective-aligned learner behaviors the debrief agent scores the transcript against. The bridge from 'doing' to 'assessment'.

evidence.description: What, in the transcript, counts as evidence the learner did this.

scoring.description: The rubric /api/score judges the transcript against and the debrief coach presents at its final stage. REQUIRED for any scenario that runs the text flow: without it /api/score returns 400 and the debrief emits no rubric. Voice scenarios (those with an ElevenLabs agent) still want one so the flow works if the agent is ever removed.

scale.description: Human-readable total range, e.g. '0-8'. Should equal 0-(2 x dimensions).

maxTotal.description: Maximum achievable total. Must equal 2 x the number of dimensions.

unlockThreshold.description: Total at or above which the learner clears the phase gate.

presentAtStage.description: The Kolb stage at which the coach may reveal the scores. Never earlier.

dimensions.description: The scored dimensions, each 0-2. Every dimension must cite a real objectiveId from the module manifest so the score maps back to the curriculum.

id.description: Stable dimension id (D1, D2, ...). Used as the JSON key the scorer returns.

objectiveId.description: The learning objective this dimension measures. Must appear in targetObjectiveIds.

name.description: Learner-facing dimension name. Must match the public brief in src/data/scenarioBriefs.ts.

levels.description: Observable criteria for each score. All three are required — the scorer quotes them verbatim.

debriefQuestion.description: A question the coach can ask to open this dimension during the debrief.

tiers.description: Total-score bands and the coaching move for each. Ranges must cover 0..maxTotal without gaps.

range.description: Inclusive band, e.g. '0-3' or a single total like '8'.

label.description: Short name shown on the score card.

coachMove.description: What the coach does at this tier.

debrief.description: Configuration for the Kolb-cycle reflection agent that runs AFTER the simulation. The agent walks the four stages in order, one focused question at a time.

model.description: The reflection framework. Kolb: Concrete Experience -> Reflective Observation -> Abstract Conceptualization -> Active Experimentation.

openingMove.description: First thing the debrief agent says when the simulation ends.

stages.description: The four Kolb stages, in order. Each gives the agent its intent and seed prompts; the agent adapts to the actual transcript.

intent.description: What this stage is trying to get the learner to do.

prompts.description: Seed questions the agent may use or adapt. Reference {successSignals} so the agent grounds reflection in what actually happened.

revealHiddenState.description: If true, the agent may disclose the relevant character.hiddenState during this stage (typically reflective-observation) so the learner can compare their reads to ground truth.

exitCriteria.description: When the debrief is considered complete (e.g. 'learner names one concrete change they will try next time').
